transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-09
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Rivera (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Jordan Patel (Lensley Platform Eng), Priya Singh (Lensley SRE), Samir Bose (Lensley ML Lead), Leah Torres (Lensley Security)

Summary:
Short check-in to validate onboarding progress: creds, service accounts, gateway rules, and first-pass KV cache warmup / latency benchmarks. Main focus on removing blockers to run the 1k-token cold-run and to align on security handoffs for KMS and SSO.

Topics: onboarding status; service account provisioning; network/gateway access; KMS & encryption; KV cache warmup and small benchmarking; SLO alignment for 95th pct latency; next steps and security deep-dive scheduling.

Action items (recorded): see metadata for owners and due dates.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, I think we have a pretty full agenda, just to run through the status and unblock the warmup benchmark, is that right Jordan?
[00:12] Jordan: yeah thanks Alex, we want to make sure the onboarding checklist is green — primarily service account + gateway rules, plus Leah wants to confirm KMS constraints before we run any prod-like data through the pilot.
[00:24] Alex: totally. Maya, do you want to give the SE view on what we need to run the 1k token prefix benchmark?
[00:30] Maya: sure, quick one — technically we need the service principal with ability to call the Redwood gateway, and we also prefer a short-lived API key for the run so we can rotate faster; we'll do streaming enabled, and capture 95th pct latency with traces. Also we want to proton the KV cache so the prefix hits aren't all cold; so a warmup script that replays a small prompt set.
[00:55] Priya: quick clarification — when you say service principal can you list the exact IAM rights? our security team insists on least privilege.
[01:03] Maya: yeah, so read/write to the gateway endpoint, ability to create ephemeral keys is optional, but mainly ability to POST inference requests, and to GET status. We don't need cluster-admin or anything like that. We'll provide a minimal JSON policy later.
[01:17] Priya: okay that helps. I'll create an IAM role tomorrow but need the exact policy.
[01:22] Alex: I'll drop the policy in the chat after the call. Jordan, are there any network egress rules that will block the gateway?
[01:29] Jordan: yup, we have an internal proxy that blocks unknown outbound endpoints; Priya is adding exception list entries. also, port ranges for the gateway TLS are standard 443 but the proxy inspects SNI.
[01:40] Priya: we need the exact hostnames or IPs — you mentioned a staging gateway, what's the FQDN?
[01:46] Maya: staging is gateway.staging.redwood-inference.com. we'll also provide a fallback IP range if DNS resolution is problematic.
[01:54] Leah: on the KMS side — we operate HSM-backed keys with policy that disallows key export. If your runtime requires direct decrypt calls we need to see the integration pattern, otherwise prefer envelope encryption where Redwood holds ephemeral keys and we store wrapped keys.
[02:08] Alex: thanks Leah, that's expected for regulated PHI workloads. Redwood supports customer-managed keys (CMK) via KMS; for Private deployments we can integrate to your KMS, but for hosted we can also use envelope encryption with HSM-wrap. We'll capture both options in the doc.
[02:24] Samir: for the benchmark we want a 1k-token prefix to approximate our clinical note generation load. Are you going to test quantized model variants? Our inference footprint matters for cost.
[02:35] Maya: good question — for the POC we'll run both the float16/base model and an int8 quantized variant. The initial warmup will use the base path, then we'll rerun with quant settings; the metrics sheet will include token/s, p95 latency, and CPU/GPU utilization snapshots.
[02:51] Jordan: will Redwood's console show token breakdown and per-route cost? we want to map cost per 1k tokens to our SaaS unit economics.
[02:58] Alex: yes, Redwood Console shows token-level cost and per-route breakdowns — we'll add a sample view to the shared deck.
[03:06] Priya: about data retention — we are not allowed to retain raw input with PHI in staging. how does the gateway handle redaction or opt-out?
[03:14] Maya: we can configure request-level retention policies; by default logs are anonymized, and there is an option to disable retention entirely for specific routes. We'll record the configuration snippet in the security doc.
[03:26] Jordan: ok that's reassuring. let's talk blockers — Priya, anything preventing service account tomorrow?
[03:32] Priya: main blocker is we need that least-priv policy and the list of gateway hostnames. Also Leah said she wants to see the KMS integration plan before approving the role for anything that touches PHI.
[03:44] Leah: also want to confirm audit logging — if Redwood uses a hosted control plane will we get audit logs forwarded to our SIEM?
[03:51] Alex: yes, we can push audit logs to your syslog or S3 with proper encryption, or we can provide role-based access to the Redwood Console's audit view. We'll include an example of the S3 forwarding pattern.
[04:03] Samir: timeline check — we'd like to run the baseline warmup and latency runs by Friday so we can analyze before the architecture review next Wednesday. Is that realistic?
[04:12] Maya: it's tight but doable if we get creds today or tomorrow. The actual warmup run takes ~45 minutes and the quantized run another 40; plus we need time to upload traces.
[04:24] Jordan: Priya, can you aim to create the role by tomorrow morning?
[04:28] Priya: yes I can try. but one more ask — do you have an automated smoke test we can peek at before the run?
[04:35] Maya: yes, we'll share a smoke test script (bash + curl) and a small prompt set; it has a dry-run mode so it doesn't hit the full model.
[04:44] Alex: I'll put both artifacts in the shared drive and ping you.
[04:47] Jordan: perfect.
[04:50] [05:00] --- 5 minute checkpoint: recap of required hostnames, policy, and KMS doc.
[05:10] Leah: one security nuance — our compliance team insists on a vulnerability scan of any third-party agent running inside our VPC. Should we plan to run the Redwood probe?
[05:19] Alex: Redwood can accept a scan against our staging gateway; we'll provide a short window. We can't allow direct scans of hosted runtime nodes, but staging gateways and any customer-managed Private gateways are fair game.
[05:32] Priya: ok then we need a scheduled window. tentative Friday 02:00–03:00 UTC?
[05:39] Alex: that works — we'll confirm blackout windows in the doc.
[05:44] Samir: when you run the quantized run, can we get peak memory and GPU util over time? we want to see whether batching yields cost wins for our prompt distribution.
[05:54] Maya: yes we'll capture GPU mem and occupancy metrics, and run with two batching configs: low-latency (batch size 1–2) and throughput (batch size up to 8) so you can see tradeoffs.
[06:06] Jordan: do you have recommendations for our SLOs? we are trying to hit 200ms p95 for single-turn generation at 512 tokens.
[06:14] Maya: 200ms p95 for 512 is aggressive on a shared hosted tier, more feasible on Dedicated or Private with pinned capacity. For the POC on staging we should set a realistic target of 350–450ms p95 on the quantized variant, and show projected improvements with a Dedicated pool.
[06:30] Leah: if we need Dedicated, we need cost estimates and an SLA.
[06:34] Alex: we'll include a Dedicated estimate and a sample SLA in the SOW.
[06:38] [10:00] Maya: small note on KV cache warmup — because your prompts share long common prefixes, the KV warmup will significantly reduce token compute. we'll show warmup effectiveness as hit-rate over time.
[10:14] Samir: that's promising. how many warmup queries do you anticipate for a 90% hit rate?
[10:20] Maya: ballpark: leveraging our continuous batching and prefix caching, 5–10k replayed prefixes should get you to ~85–90% hit on typical note templates; we'll measure and refine.
[10:33] Jordan: ok makes sense. one more infra question — do we need special VPC peering for Private?
[10:40] Alex: for Private yes, we can support VPC peering or VPN; for hosted we rely on TLS-only gateway endpoints and standard egress. We'll outline network diagrams for both.
[10:49] Leah: regarding data residency, some customers require EU-only keys. our pilot doesn't require that but it's good to understand options.
[10:57] Alex: noted, Redwood supports region pinning per deployment for Dedicated/Private.
[11:02] Priya: quick ops question — if our pipeline has a spike in traffic, is there an automatic fallback to a cheaper model or region? we want graceful degradation not abrupt failures.
[11:11] Maya: yes, we can set routing policies: fallback to a smaller model, or to a lower-tier capacity pool. Redwood has automated fallback policies that can be configured per-route with thresholds.
[11:22] Jordan: those sound helpful. let's talk about the smoke test and its expected outputs, Maya?
[11:28] Maya: smoke test produces a small JSON with request/response times, token counts, and a trace id. It logs whether KV hit occurred. We'll include a sample log.
[11:38] [15:00] Jordan: security acceptance criteria — Leah, what else do you need to sign off to allow pilot to run on staging with synthetic PHI?
[15:45] Leah: I need: (1) KMS integration pattern and guarantee no key export; (2) audit logging forwarded to our SIEM; (3) least-priv role and a scan window for vuln scanning; (4) a data retention policy that zeros retention for the route. Once those are on paper I can sign off.
[16:12] Alex: we'll bundle all four items in the security pack and route it to you as a single doc.
[16:20] Priya: timeline again — when can we expect the policy and hostnames?
[16:24] Alex: by EOD — I'll send the IAM policy and the hostnames list as a short snippet, plus the smoke test and the SOW stub.
[16:31] Samir: if you can add an exemplar metrics view for token-cost mapping that would help our finance team.
[16:38] Alex: yes, I'll add one and include an example price calc.
[16:43] Maya: on the bench run — two more details: we'll run with pinned context length of 1024 to match your notes, and we'll capture 95 and 99 pct latencies. We'll supply an anonymized CSV of results.
[16:57] Jordan: what UI access will Samir and I have to the Redwood Console? read-only?
[17:02] Alex: we'll grant read-only access for both, and a cross-team view for Leah for audit logs.
[17:08] Leah: and for the SSO, we require SAML metadata exchange before any UI access.
[17:13] Alex: we'll initiate the SAML metadata handoff today.
[17:17] [20:00] --- midway recap: hostnames, IAM policy, KMS doc, smoke script, scheduled vuln scan window, warmup run by Friday.
[20:20] Priya: note on firewall — our proxy does TLS terminating and will rewrite SNI, so if you rely on SNI for routing it might break. Is there a mutual TLS option?
[20:33] Maya: we do support mTLS for Private and for a gateway adjacency setup. For hosted staging gateway, mTLS is more complex because we manage cert rotation. We'll propose both options in the doc.
[20:47] Samir: let's keep mTLS as plan B; for now we'll try regular TLS with pinned hostnames.
[20:54] Alex: fair. I'll mark mTLS as optional.
[20:58] Jordan: any blockers on Redwood side that would delay this week?
[21:02] Maya: none — our infra team is ready, just need credentials and the go-ahead for the scan window.
[21:08] Alex: I'll coordinate the vuln scan window with infra and get back by EOD.
[21:12] [30:00] Maya: quick note on metrics — I'll include a small dashboard template for p95/p99 and token cost, plus a CSV schema so you can feed it into your internal dashboards.
[30:18] Samir: great, can you include a projected cost per 1M tokens for the quantized path?
[30:24] Alex: yes, we'll provide sample cost numbers for hosted and Dedicated, and an estimate for on-prem Private if needed.
[30:30] Leah: ok one last security question — will any logs include raw prompts in plaintext? we must avoid storing PHI.
[30:37] Maya: logs will be redacted by default; the smoke test dry-run has a flag that avoids sending raw prompt text to logs.
[30:45] Jordan: that's good. 
[30:48] [40:00] Alex: let's do a quick risk checklist: networking, svc account, KMS, vuln scan, API keys rotation, and budgeting. Any additional risks?
[40:09] Leah: legal should review the SOW for data processing addendums.
[40:14] Alex: we'll attach DPA language to the SOW.
[40:18] Priya: Ops risk — we want circuit-breaker thresholds configured so spikes won't exhaust capacity.
[40:25] Maya: we can preconfigure circuit-breakers on your route with rate limits and automatic model-fallback.
[40:31] Jordan: awesome. Any final items?
[40:35] Samir: none from product.
[40:37] Leah: I just want the security doc by Monday.
[40:41] Alex: we can do Monday EOD, noted.
[40:45] [46:20] Recap and next steps:
- Alex will upload IAM policy, hostnames, smoke script, and SOW stub by EOD (2027-09-09).
- Priya will attempt to create service principal and confirm by 2027-09-11.
- Maya will run KV warmup + baseline latency runs once creds available and share CSV by 2027-09-14.
- Leah will review security pack and list compliance docs by 2027-09-13.
- Schedule security deep-dive for 2027-09-16 (TBD)

End of call.
